findings.text: follow-on: the successor traversal is capped at HAS_SUCCESSOR*0..25, so a chain deeper than 25 returns a truncated identity set and an identity the cut publishes beyond the cap evades the very refusal this change closes; the sibling owner fetch_manifest_source_release_rows (graph_ops.py:12975) traverses the same relationship unbounded, so the 25 is unexplained and the guard fails open at its boundary.

item_verdicts.call_sites: The production call sites reaching the change are imas_codex/cli/sn.py:4527 (_run_export_cli), imas_codex/cli/sn.py:4658 (the no-argument export path) and imas_codex/standard_names/catalog_release.py:2290 (the release gate wrapper), each of which calls run_export; the new helper and the extended _source_disposition are reachable only through run_export, and the node's own test file is not counted.
item_verdicts.diff: Read commit-by-commit against base 345868c92: the one commit 912e92aa3 changes imas_codex/standard_names/export.py (+95/-12 - _refuse_waiver_that_reached_a_name now takes landed_identities, new _fetch_waived_source_chain_identities at :2789, _source_disposition gains chain_identities at :2834, and both run_export call sites pass waived_manifest_source_chain_identities at :3424/:3531), adds tests/standard_names/test_export_waiver_intermediates.py (+206) and docs/evidence/fragments/sn-integrity-backlog/sib-export-waiver-intermediates.html (+36). No production file the goal does not name is touched.
item_verdicts.done_when: The done_when asks for a refused published-intermediate case, an all-unwaived chain that passes, a reversion log with EXIT=, and no added failure in test_export_release_holds.py. tests/standard_names/test_export_waiver_intermediates.py carries four tests (two refusal at :45 and :184, two non-refusal); negative-control.log reproduces the two refusal tests red at EXIT=1; after-export-tests.log shows 7 failed / 105 passed against base-export-tests.log's 7 failed / 101 passed with the identical seven ids, so test_export_release_holds.py adds no failure.
item_verdicts.goal: The node goal is that the export waiver refusal weigh every identity a waived source's chain would publish, not only the terminal, from imas_codex/standard_names/export.py. The landed change does exactly that: _fetch_waived_source_chain_identities (:2789) reads the source's produced name and every name reachable along HAS_SUCCESSOR, and _source_disposition (:2834/:2845) refuses on any identity in that set that the cut publishes.
item_verdicts.manifest: Read at /home/ITER/mcintos/.reckon/crew/runs/r-20261012T185758425051-sib-export-waiver-intermediates/manifest.md; it records status complete, the single commit 912e92aa3, the three changed paths, the baseline/after/negative arms with log paths, measurement_module and measurement_cwd, and the four added tests. Every claim I checked (the diff scope, the two arm logs' identical failure ids, the negative-control log, the fragment text) held; the one caveat is that after-export-tests.log's own body line records revision 345868c92 (dirty worktree) while the manifest's after_suite JSON records 912e92aa3.
item_verdicts.write_paths: The manifest declares imas_codex/standard_names/export.py, tests/standard_names/test_export_waiver_intermediates.py and docs/evidence/fragments/sn-integrity-backlog/sib-export-waiver-intermediates.html; git diff --stat 345868c92..912e92aa3 reports exactly those three files (325 insertions, 12 deletions) and no generated model or gitignored file is staged.

justifications.durability: The two refusal tests are durable because negative-control.log shows them red with the chain branch reverted (export.py:2845) and green at head: test_a_waived_source_whose_chain_publishes_an_intermediate_refuses passes chain_identities={intermediate, terminal} and asserts the raised message names the intermediate, which a terminal-only build cannot produce, and test_the_cut_refuses_a_waived_source_whose_intermediate_is_published reddens when the chain is ignored; both were observed failing in the reversion arm. Score 18 not 20 because the traversal is capped at HAS_SUCCESSOR*0..25 (export.py:2817) and no test exercises a chain at that boundary, so a chain deeper than the cap fails open; the message assertions themselves are not tautological, since each compares the code's rendered output against an identity the code had to select and name.
justifications.evidence: Read receipts, not absence of error. base-export-tests.log and after-export-tests.log each open with '# revision=... tree=...', '# command=...' and 'cwd:'/'module:' header lines and end with 'EXIT=1' after '7 failed, 101 passed' and '7 failed, 105 passed'; the two FAILED id lists are identical, so added_failure_count is 0. negative-control.log opens at revision 912e92aa3 and ends 'EXIT=1' after '2 failed, 2 passed', failing exactly the two refusal tests the head arm passes. Score 18 not 20 because the after arm's own body records revision 345868c92 with 'dirty worktree: export.py modified', so that arm is provably the working tree, not the commit.
justifications.fit: The change matches its surroundings: _fetch_waived_source_chain_identities (:2789) mirrors the module's existing fetch-and-return-mapping idiom and keeps its Cypher beside the caller per the sprint rule, _refuse... — _refuse_waiver_that_reached_a_name (:2759) keeps a single refusal path rather than adding a second check, and no symbol, filename or comment carries a plan, section, gate or ticket label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: export.py:2845 computes 'reached' from {standard_name_id, *(chain_identities or ())} intersected with exported_ids and calls the one refusal when the set is non-empty; the two run_export call sites (:3424 over the published set, :3531 over exported_ids) each pass waived_manifest_source_chain_identities.get(...) read once before any staging output at :2966, so a waived source whose chain published an intermediate is refused. Score 19 not 20 because the fix is latent (no declared-waived source currently produces an identity) and the depth cap at :2817 leaves one boundary unguarded.
justifications.reuse: I searched imas_codex/standard_names for an existing full chain-set lookup (graph_ops.py:12909 fetch_manifest_source_release_rows, graph_ops.py:12973, search.py:693) and found every owner resolves only the terminal identity; no owner of the 'every identity a manifest source's chain carries' capability exists, and the new helper reuses the same 'dd:'+path key and PRODUCED_NAME relationship as that owner while adding the bounded-depth member set, so it extends the idiom rather than duplicating a capability. Score 19 not 20 because it does not extend fetch_manifest_source_release_rows itself, which now shares a near-identical traversal statement.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat 345868c92..912e92aa3 reports exactly the three declared paths - imas_codex/standard_names/export.py, tests/standard_names/test_export_waiver_intermediates.py, and docs/evidence/fragments/sn-integrity-backlog/sib-export-waiver-intermediates.html - with 325 insertions and 12 deletions, no generated model staged and nothing the goal does not imply.
